title.ro: De ce o Biblioteca Standard de Template-uri?

question.en: Every C++ program needs the same handful of data structures: resizable arrays, linked lists, key-value maps, FIFO queues, formatted streams, mutable strings. Without a standard library, every team writes its own — incompatible, untested, leaky. What does the language community owe its users to break this cycle?
question.ro: Orice program C++ are nevoie de aceleasi structuri de date: tablouri redimensionabile, liste inlantuite, dictionare cheie-valoare, cozi FIFO, fluxuri formatate, siruri modificabile. Fara o biblioteca standard, fiecare echipa scrie variante proprii — incompatibile, netestate, cu scurgeri. Ce datoreaza comunitatea limbajului utilizatorilor pentru a rupe acest ciclu?

answer.en: A reusable set of templates with a stable interface: STL (Standard Template Library). Containers, iterators, algorithms, adaptors, allocators — all generic, all interoperable. Course 7 is the tour.
answer.ro: Un set reutilizabil de template-uri cu o interfata stabila: STL (Standard Template Library). Containere, iteratori, algoritmi, adaptori, alocatori — toate generice, toate interoperabile. Cursul 7 este turul lor.

content.en:
Course 7 covers six interlocking topics of STL part 1:
- **Sequence containers** — `vector`, `deque`, `array`, `list`, `forward_list`
- **Container adaptors** — `stack`, `queue`, `priority_queue` (built on top of a sequence container)
- **I/O streams** — the `iostream` hierarchy, manipulators, file I/O, binary mode
- **Strings** — `basic_string`, `char_traits`, `string_view` (C++17)
- **Initialization lists** — `initializer_list`, brace-init, variadic macros
- **Iterators** — categories per container, invalidation rules, reverse iteration
content.ro:
Cursul 7 acopera sase teme interdependente din STL partea I:
- **Containere secventiale** — `vector`, `deque`, `array`, `list`, `forward_list`
- **Adaptori de container** — `stack`, `queue`, `priority_queue` (construiti peste un container secvential)
- **Fluxuri I/O** — ierarhia `iostream`, manipulatori, I/O pe fisiere, mod binar
- **Siruri** — `basic_string`, `char_traits`, `string_view` (C++17)
- **Liste de initializare** — `initializer_list`, brace-init, macro-uri variadice
- **Iteratori** — categorii pe container, reguli de invalidare, iterare inversa

content.en: STL is a set of **templates** organized into five buckets: containers (class templates that hold other classes), iterators (pointer-like objects for traversal), algorithms (free functions usable across containers), adaptors (wrappers that re-expose a container with a different interface), and allocators (memory-policy hooks). To use any of them, include the header and reach for them via `std::` (or pull the namespace in with `using namespace std;`).
content.ro: STL este un set de **template-uri** organizate in cinci categorii: containere (template-uri de clase care contin alte clase), iteratori (obiecte de tip pointer pentru parcurgere), algoritmi (functii libere ce functioneaza peste containere), adaptori (wrappere care reexpun un container cu alta interfata) si alocatori (carlige pentru politica de memorie). Pentru a le folosi, include header-ul si refera-le via `std::` (sau aduce namespace-ul cu `using namespace std;`).

content.en: STL implementations are compiler-specific. The interface is fixed by the standard, but the underlying data structures (e.g., `vector` growth factor, `unordered_map` bucket policy) vary between MSVC, GCC, and Clang. Performance numbers in this course are MSVC-measured; expect the curve shape to be similar elsewhere but exact figures to differ.
content.ro: Implementarile STL sunt specifice compilatorului. Interfata este fixata de standard, dar structurile de date interne (de ex. factorul de crestere `vector`, politica bucket-urilor `unordered_map`) variaza intre MSVC, GCC si Clang. Numerele de performanta din acest curs sunt masurate pe MSVC; asteapta-te ca forma curbei sa fie similara, iar cifrele exacte sa difere.

question.en: You have to store `1,000,000` integers, and you do not know up front how many will actually arrive. You want random access (read element `i` in O(1)) and amortized cheap append. Which standard container is the default choice — and what is the hidden cost you accept in exchange?
question.ro: Trebuie sa stochezi `1.000.000` de intregi, fara sa stii dinainte cati vor sosi efectiv. Vrei acces aleator (citire element `i` in O(1)) si append amortizat ieftin. Ce container standard este alegerea implicita — si care este costul ascuns pe care il accepti in schimb?

answer.en: `std::vector<int>`. The hidden cost is **reallocation**: when `push_back` outgrows the current capacity, the vector allocates a larger buffer, **copies/moves every existing element**, then frees the old buffer. Each individual `push_back` is O(1) amortized, but a single one can cost O(n) when it triggers a grow.
answer.ro: `std::vector<int>`. Costul ascuns este **realocarea**: cand `push_back` depaseste capacitatea curenta, vectorul aloca un buffer mai mare, **copiaza/muta fiecare element existent**, apoi elibereaza buffer-ul vechi. Fiecare `push_back` individual este O(1) amortizat, dar unul singur poate costa O(n) cand declanseaza o crestere.

content.en:
**Three traps to flag up front about `vector`:**
1. *Every `push_back` is cheap.* No — without `reserve()`, periodic reallocations copy every element. The professor's `Vec-1` (no reserve) measured `1936 ms` average vs `Vec-2` (with reserve) at `517 ms` — a ~4x cost on the same workload.
2. *`v[i]` and `v.at(i)` are equivalent.* No — `operator[]` does NO bounds check in Release; `at()` throws `std::out_of_range`. Mixing them up turns a debug-only crash into a Release-build silent corruption.
3. *Pushing an object into a vector keeps a reference to the original.* No — `push_back` makes a **copy**. Mutating the original after pushing does not change what is in the vector.
content.ro:
**Trei capcane de semnalat de la inceput despre `vector`:**
1. *Orice `push_back` este ieftin.* Nu — fara `reserve()`, realocari periodice copiaza fiecare element. `Vec-1` al profesorului (fara reserve) a masurat `1936 ms` in medie, fata de `Vec-2` (cu reserve) la `517 ms` — un cost de ~4x pe aceeasi sarcina.
2. *`v[i]` si `v.at(i)` sunt echivalente.* Nu — `operator[]` NU verifica limitele in Release; `at()` arunca `std::out_of_range`. Confuzia transforma un crash de debug intr-o coruptie tacuta in Release.
3. *Adaugarea unui obiect in vector pastreaza o referinta la original.* Nu — `push_back` face o **copie**. Modificarea originalului dupa adaugare nu schimba ce este in vector.

content.en:
A `vector<T>` is a unidimensional, contiguously stored, dynamically resized array of `T`. Memory allocation and resizing happen automatically. **Every object you `push_back` is stored as a copy** of the original — mutating the original afterwards does not change the vector's content.

The four operation families are: **insertion** (`push_back`, `insert`), **deletion** (`pop_back`, `erase`, `clear`), **reallocation control** (`resize`, `reserve`), **access** (`operator[]`, `at()`, `front()`, `back()`, `data()`).
content.ro:
Un `vector<T>` este un tablou unidimensional, stocat contiguu, redimensionat dinamic, de elemente `T`. Alocarea memoriei si redimensionarea se intampla automat. **Fiecare obiect pe care faci `push_back` este stocat ca o copie** a originalului — modificarea originalului ulterior nu schimba continutul vectorului.

Cele patru familii de operatii sunt: **inserare** (`push_back`, `insert`), **stergere** (`pop_back`, `erase`, `clear`), **control al realocarii** (`resize`, `reserve`), **acces** (`operator[]`, `at()`, `front()`, `back()`, `data()`).

content.en: Four-step sequence triggered when `push_back` would exceed the current capacity: (1) allocate a larger contiguous buffer (typical strategy: doubling under GCC/Clang, ~1.5x under MSVC), (2) copy or move-construct each existing element into the new buffer, (3) destroy + free the old buffer, (4) copy/move the newly pushed element into the extra slot. Cost is O(n) for the single push that triggers it; amortized O(1) per push across the lifetime of the vector.
content.ro: Secventa in patru pasi declansata cand `push_back` ar depasi capacitatea curenta: (1) aloca un buffer contiguu mai mare (strategie tipica: dublare sub GCC/Clang, ~1.5x sub MSVC), (2) copiaza sau muta-construieste fiecare element existent in noul buffer, (3) distruge + elibereaza buffer-ul vechi, (4) copiaza/muta elementul abia adaugat in slotul extra. Costul este O(n) pentru push-ul care o declanseaza; amortizat O(1) per push pe durata de viata a vectorului.

rows.en: Pointers move cheaply; objects allocated on heap.
rows.ro: Pointerii se muta ieftin; obiectele alocate pe heap.

rows.en: Best for heavy objects with cheap pointer semantics.
rows.ro: Cel mai bun pentru obiecte grele cu semantica ieftina de pointer.

items.en: **`capacity()`** — slots pre-allocated; `>= size()`. Reserve to avoid reallocations.
items.ro: **`capacity()`** — sloturi pre-alocate; `>= size()`. Foloseste reserve pentru a evita realocari.

items.en: **`max_size()`** — theoretical upper bound (depends on allocator + addressing).
items.ro: **`max_size()`** — limita superioara teoretica (depinde de alocator + adresare).

items.en: **`empty()`** — `true` when `size() == 0`. Prefer over `size() == 0` (clearer + works on every container).
items.ro: **`empty()`** — `true` cand `size() == 0`. Prefera-l fata de `size() == 0` (mai clar + functioneaza pe orice container).

items.en: **`data()`** — raw `T*` pointer to the contiguous storage. C++11 addition; the only way to feed a `vector` into a legacy C API.
items.ro: **`data()`** — pointer brut `T*` catre stocarea contigua. Adaugat in C++11; singura cale de a trimite un `vector` catre un API C clasic.

content.en: Vector relational operators (`==`, `<`) require the element type to define `const operator==` and `const operator<`. Equality compares element-by-element; `<` does a lexicographic compare. `operator!=` and `operator>` are derived from `==` and `<`, so you do NOT need to define them.
content.ro: Operatorii relationali ai vectorului (`==`, `<`) cer ca tipul elementului sa defineasca `const operator==` si `const operator<`. Egalitatea compara element cu element; `<` face o comparatie lexicografica. `operator!=` si `operator>` sunt derivati din `==` si `<`, deci NU trebuie definiti.

question.en: You profile a workload that builds a `vector<T>` of 1,000,000 heavy objects in a tight loop. Without `reserve()`, the program spends `1936 ms` average; with `reserve(1000000)` before the loop, it drops to `517 ms`. Where did the saved 1419 ms go?
question.ro: Profilezi o sarcina ce construieste un `vector<T>` cu 1.000.000 de obiecte grele intr-o bucla stransa. Fara `reserve()`, programul ia `1936 ms` in medie; cu `reserve(1000000)` inainte de bucla, scade la `517 ms`. Unde au disparut cele 1419 ms economisite?

answer.en: Into the avoided reallocations. Without reserve, the vector grows ~30 times during one million pushes (each growth ~doubles capacity), and each growth copy-constructs every existing element into a new buffer + destroys the old one. With reserve, the buffer is sized exactly once at the start and every `push_back` is a single placement — no copying of pre-existing elements, no allocator round-trips.
answer.ro: In realocarile evitate. Fara reserve, vectorul creste de ~30 de ori pe parcursul unui milion de adaugari (fiecare crestere ~dubleaza capacitatea), iar fiecare crestere copiaza-construieste fiecare element existent intr-un buffer nou si distruge buffer-ul vechi. Cu reserve, buffer-ul este dimensionat exact o data la inceput si fiecare `push_back` este o singura plasare — fara copii de elemente preexistente, fara apeluri la alocator.

question.en: You write `vector<Integer> v; Integer i(5); v.push_back(i); i.Set(6);` then print `v[0].Get()`. What does it print, and why?
question.ro: Scrii `vector<Integer> v; Integer i(5); v.push_back(i); i.Set(6);` apoi tiparesti `v[0].Get()`. Ce afiseaza si de ce?

text.en: `5` — `push_back` invoked the copy constructor; `v[0]` is an independent object from `i`
text.ro: `5` — `push_back` a invocat constructorul de copiere; `v[0]` este un obiect independent de `i`

explanation.en: Correct — every object added to a vector is stored as a COPY. The original `i` and `v[0]` are unrelated after `push_back`; mutating one does not affect the other.
explanation.ro: Corect — fiecare obiect adaugat intr-un vector este stocat ca o COPIE. Originalul `i` si `v[0]` sunt fara legatura dupa `push_back`; modificarea unuia nu il afecteaza pe celalalt.

text.en: `6` — `push_back` stores a reference to `i`, so changes to `i` are visible in `v`
text.ro: `6` — `push_back` stocheaza o referinta la `i`, deci modificarile lui `i` sunt vizibile in `v`

explanation.en: No — vector containers store values, not references. `push_back(i)` calls `Integer`'s copy constructor and stores a fully independent object.
explanation.ro: Nu — containerele vector stocheaza valori, nu referinte. `push_back(i)` apeleaza constructorul de copiere al `Integer` si stocheaza un obiect complet independent.

text.en: Undefined behaviour — modifying `i` after `push_back` invalidates `v[0]`
text.ro: Comportament nedefinit — modificarea lui `i` dupa `push_back` invalideaza `v[0]`

explanation.en: No — `v[0]` and `i` are independent objects with their own lifetimes. Mutating one is perfectly defined and has zero effect on the other.
explanation.ro: Nu — `v[0]` si `i` sunt obiecte independente cu propriile durate de viata. Modificarea unuia este perfect definita si nu are niciun efect asupra celuilalt.

text.en: Compile error — `Integer` does not have a move constructor
text.ro: Eroare de compilare — `Integer` nu are constructor de mutare

explanation.en: No — a copy constructor alone is enough for `push_back`. Move is an optimization, not a requirement.
explanation.ro: Nu — un constructor de copiere singur este suficient pentru `push_back`. Mutarea este o optimizare, nu o cerinta.

explanation.en: The 'vector stores copies' principle is the most common surprise for newcomers. It explains why heavy types are usually held by smart-pointer (`vector<unique_ptr<T>>`) rather than by value when you need shared ownership.
explanation.ro: Principiul 'vector stocheaza copii' este cea mai frecventa surpriza pentru incepatori. Explica de ce tipurile grele sunt de obicei pastrate prin pointer inteligent (`vector<unique_ptr<T>>`) si nu prin valoare cand ai nevoie de proprietate partajata.

question.en: You measure two implementations: `Vec-1` (1,000,000 `push_back` calls, no `reserve`) costs `1936 ms`; `Vec-2` (same workload + `reserve(1000000)` first) costs `517 ms`. What is the root cause of the ~4x speedup?
question.ro: Masori doua implementari: `Vec-1` (1.000.000 de apeluri `push_back`, fara `reserve`) costa `1936 ms`; `Vec-2` (aceeasi sarcina + `reserve(1000000)` la inceput) costa `517 ms`. Care este cauza radacina a accelerarii de ~4x?

text.en: Avoided reallocations — without `reserve`, the buffer grows ~30 times and each growth copies every existing element to a new buffer.
text.ro: Realocari evitate — fara `reserve`, buffer-ul creste de ~30 de ori si fiecare crestere copiaza fiecare element existent intr-un buffer nou.

explanation.en: Correct — `reserve` pays the allocation cost once. Each subsequent `push_back` becomes a placement into pre-allocated space, with no copy of pre-existing elements and no allocator round-trip.
explanation.ro: Corect — `reserve` plateste costul alocarii o singura data. Fiecare `push_back` ulterior devine o plasare in spatiul pre-alocat, fara copii ale elementelor preexistente si fara apeluri la alocator.

text.en: `reserve` enables compiler vectorization of `push_back`, doubling instruction throughput
text.ro: `reserve` activeaza vectorizarea automata a `push_back`, dubland debitul de instructiuni

explanation.en: No — `reserve` is a runtime allocator call, not a compiler hint for SIMD. The win is allocator + copy avoidance.
explanation.ro: Nu — `reserve` este un apel de alocator la runtime, nu o sugestie pentru compilator pentru SIMD. Castigul este evitarea alocarii si copierii.

text.en: `reserve` switches the vector to a different (faster) container type internally
text.ro: `reserve` schimba intern vectorul cu un alt tip de container (mai rapid)

explanation.en: No — `reserve` does not change the container type. It only resizes the underlying allocation in place.
explanation.ro: Nu — `reserve` nu schimba tipul containerului. Doar redimensioneaza alocarea interna pe loc.

text.en: `reserve` enables cache prefetching that is otherwise disabled
text.ro: `reserve` activeaza pre-incarcare in cache care altfel este dezactivata

explanation.en: No — vectors are always contiguous in memory; cache prefetching applies equally before and after `reserve`. The 4x gap is allocator + copy work, not cache behaviour.
explanation.ro: Nu — vectorii sunt mereu contigui in memorie; pre-incarcarea in cache se aplica la fel inainte si dupa `reserve`. Diferenta de 4x este in alocator + copiere, nu in comportamentul cache-ului.

explanation.en: The Vec-1 / Vec-2 numbers are concrete evidence for why `reserve` is the default first step in any tight insertion loop with known target size.
explanation.ro: Numerele Vec-1 / Vec-2 sunt dovezi concrete pentru care `reserve` este primul pas implicit in orice bucla stransa de inserare cu dimensiune tinta cunoscuta.

question.en: In a Release build, `v[100000]` and `v.at(100000)` on a vector of size 50 behave how?
question.ro: Intr-un build Release, `v[100000]` si `v.at(100000)` pe un vector de dimensiune 50 se comporta cum?

text.en: `v[100000]` is undefined behaviour (no bounds check); `v.at(100000)` throws `std::out_of_range`
text.ro: `v[100000]` este comportament nedefinit (fara verificare de limite); `v.at(100000)` arunca `std::out_of_range`

explanation.en: Correct — `operator[]` performs no bounds check in Release; out-of-range access reads past the buffer (UB). `at()` always bounds-checks and throws `std::out_of_range` on failure. Prefer `at()` when index validity is not provable at the call site.
explanation.ro: Corect — `operator[]` nu verifica limitele in Release; un acces in afara intervalului citeste dincolo de buffer (UB). `at()` verifica intotdeauna limitele si arunca `std::out_of_range` la esec. Prefera `at()` cand validitatea indexului nu este demonstrabila la locul apelului.

text.en: Both throw `std::out_of_range`
text.ro: Ambele arunca `std::out_of_range`

explanation.en: No — `operator[]` does not bounds-check in Release. It is `at()` alone that throws.
explanation.ro: Nu — `operator[]` nu verifica limitele in Release. Doar `at()` arunca.

text.en: Both are undefined behaviour — bounds checks are off in Release
text.ro: Ambele sunt comportament nedefinit — verificarile de limite sunt oprite in Release

explanation.en: No — `at()` is required by the standard to throw regardless of build mode. Only `operator[]` is unchecked.
explanation.ro: Nu — `at()` este obligata de standard sa arunce indiferent de modul de build. Doar `operator[]` este neverificat.

text.en: `v[100000]` returns a default-constructed element; `v.at(100000)` does the same
text.ro: `v[100000]` returneaza un element construit implicit; `v.at(100000)` face la fel

explanation.en: No — vector never default-constructs elements outside its size. `operator[]` reads garbage memory (UB); `at()` throws.
explanation.ro: Nu — vector nu construieste niciodata elemente implicit in afara dimensiunii sale. `operator[]` citeste memorie aleatoare (UB); `at()` arunca.

explanation.en: The bounds-check gap between `[]` and `at()` is the most common Release-only crash source in student code. The cost of `at()` is one branch — pay it whenever the index isn't trivially in range.
explanation.ro: Diferenta de verificare a limitelor intre `[]` si `at()` este cea mai frecventa sursa de crash doar in Release in codul studentilor. Costul lui `at()` este o ramura — plateste-l ori de cate ori indexul nu este trivial in interval.

question.en: You need a container that supports cheap insertion at BOTH ends (`push_front` and `push_back`). `vector` only has `push_back`, and `push_front` on a vector is O(n) because every existing element must shift. What standard sequence container is purpose-built for this?
question.ro: Ai nevoie de un container ce suporta inserare ieftina la AMBELE capete (`push_front` si `push_back`). `vector` are doar `push_back`, iar `push_front` pe un vector este O(n) deoarece fiecare element existent trebuie deplasat. Ce container secvential standard este conceput exact pentru asta?

answer.en: `std::deque` (double-ended queue). It exposes `push_front` and `push_back` (and the matching `pop_front`/`pop_back`), both amortized O(1). Internally it stores a directory of fixed-size blocks, so it sacrifices contiguous storage in exchange for O(1) at both ends.
answer.ro: `std::deque` (coada cu doua capete). Expune `push_front` si `push_back` (si `pop_front`/`pop_back` corespunzatoare), ambele amortizate O(1). Intern, stocheaza un director de blocuri de dimensiune fixa, deci sacrifica stocarea contigua in schimbul O(1) la ambele capete.

content.en:
**Two traps about `deque` and `array`:**
1. *`deque` is contiguous like `vector`.* No — `deque` stores a directory of pointers to fixed-size chunks. Elements are NOT consecutive in memory, so **`data()`, `reserve()`, `capacity()` do NOT exist on `deque`** — there is no single contiguous buffer to expose.
2. *`std::array` is just a typedef for a C-style array.* No — `std::array<T, N>` is a value-semantic class with `begin()`, `end()`, `at()`, `size()`, full STL iterator support, and pass-by-value semantics. The C array `T[N]` decays to a pointer the moment you pass it; `std::array` does not.
content.ro:
**Doua capcane despre `deque` si `array`:**
1. *`deque` este contiguu ca `vector`.* Nu — `deque` stocheaza un director de pointeri catre bucati de dimensiune fixa. Elementele NU sunt consecutive in memorie, deci **`data()`, `reserve()`, `capacity()` NU exista pe `deque`** — nu este un singur buffer contiguu de expus.
2. *`std::array` este doar un typedef pentru un tablou C clasic.* Nu — `std::array<T, N>` este o clasa cu semantica valorica avand `begin()`, `end()`, `at()`, `size()`, suport complet pentru iteratori STL si semantica de pass-by-value. Tabloul C `T[N]` se transforma in pointer in momentul in care il transmiti; `std::array` nu.

content.en:
A `deque<T>` stores elements in a directory of fixed-size memory chunks. This makes `push_front` and `push_back` both O(1) amortized — there is no single buffer to relocate when one end grows. The trade-off: there is no single contiguous storage, so the methods that promise contiguity (`data()`, `reserve()`, `capacity()`) are removed from the interface.

`std::array<T, N>` (C++11) is a fixed-size container — size baked into the type at compile time. It is the value-semantic replacement for C-style arrays: you can pass it by value, copy it, return it from a function. It exposes the same iterator interface as the other sequence containers but offers no `push_back` / `pop_back` / `insert` / `erase` — its size is immutable.
content.ro:
Un `deque<T>` stocheaza elementele intr-un director de bucati de memorie de dimensiune fixa. Asta face `push_front` si `push_back` ambele O(1) amortizat — nu exista un singur buffer de relocat cand un capat creste. Compromisul: nu exista o stocare contigua singura, deci metodele care promit contiguitate (`data()`, `reserve()`, `capacity()`) sunt eliminate din interfata.

`std::array<T, N>` (C++11) este un container de dimensiune fixa — dimensiunea este fixata in tip la compilare. Este inlocuitorul cu semantica valorica pentru tablourile clasice C: il poti transmite prin valoare, copia, returna dintr-o functie. Expune aceeasi interfata de iteratori ca celelalte containere secventiale, dar nu ofera `push_back` / `pop_back` / `insert` / `erase` — dimensiunea sa este imutabila.

content.en: Microsoft-specific preprocessor macro controlling how aggressively the STL bounds-checks `operator[]` and iterator operations. Values: `0` = Release (no checks, fastest), `1` = Release with `_SECURE_SCL` (bounds checks added), `2` = Debug (full iterator debugging — dangling iterator detection, range checks, container compatibility). Note this is an MSVC implementation detail; GCC libstdc++ and Clang libc++ have their own debug modes (`_GLIBCXX_DEBUG`, `_LIBCPP_DEBUG`).
content.ro: Macro de preprocesor specific Microsoft care controleaza cat de agresiv verifica STL-ul limitele la `operator[]` si la operatiile pe iteratori. Valori: `0` = Release (fara verificari, cel mai rapid), `1` = Release cu `_SECURE_SCL` (verificari de limite adaugate), `2` = Debug (debugging complet al iteratorilor — detectie iteratori invalizi, verificari de interval, compatibilitate intre containere). Acesta este un detaliu de implementare MSVC; libstdc++ (GCC) si libc++ (Clang) au propriile moduri de debug (`_GLIBCXX_DEBUG`, `_LIBCPP_DEBUG`).

rows.ro: Da — plus verificari de validitate a iteratorilor

question.en: Why does `std::deque` deliberately exclude `data()`, `reserve()`, and `capacity()` from its interface? `vector` has them — why not just copy the API?
question.ro: De ce `std::deque` exclude deliberat `data()`, `reserve()` si `capacity()` din interfata? `vector` le are — de ce sa nu copieze pur si simplu API-ul?

answer.en: Those three methods all assume a SINGLE CONTIGUOUS buffer: `data()` returns a `T*` to the whole sequence, `capacity()` reports its size, `reserve()` resizes it. `deque` stores its elements in a directory of fixed-size chunks, so there is no single buffer to return, size, or grow. Adding those methods would force `deque` to either lie (return an unusable pointer) or copy elements into a temporary buffer on demand (defeating the data structure's whole purpose). The interface honestly reflects the layout.
answer.ro: Acele trei metode presupun toate un SINGUR buffer CONTIGUU: `data()` returneaza un `T*` catre intreaga secventa, `capacity()` raporteaza dimensiunea acestuia, `reserve()` il redimensioneaza. `deque` stocheaza elementele intr-un director de bucati de dimensiune fixa, deci nu este un singur buffer de returnat, dimensionat sau crescut. Adaugarea acestor metode ar forta `deque` fie sa minta (returneaza un pointer inutilizabil), fie sa copieze elementele intr-un buffer temporar la cerere (anuland scopul structurii de date). Interfata reflecta cinstit layout-ul.

question.en: Which sequence container can do `push_front` in O(1) amortized AND `data()` to expose a contiguous `T*`?
question.ro: Care container secvential poate face `push_front` in O(1) amortizat SI `data()` pentru a expune un `T*` contiguu?

text.en: Neither — `vector` has `data()` but no cheap `push_front`; `deque` has cheap `push_front` but no `data()`
text.ro: Niciunul — `vector` are `data()` dar fara `push_front` ieftin; `deque` are `push_front` ieftin dar fara `data()`

explanation.en: Correct — the two properties are physically incompatible. Cheap `push_front` requires a non-contiguous layout (directory of chunks for `deque`, or linked nodes for `list`), and `data()` requires a contiguous one. You pick one or the other.
explanation.ro: Corect — cele doua proprietati sunt fizic incompatibile. `push_front` ieftin necesita un layout non-contiguu (director de bucati pentru `deque` sau noduri inlantuite pentru `list`), iar `data()` necesita unul contiguu. Alegi unul sau altul.

text.en: `vector`
text.ro: `vector`

explanation.en: No — `vector::push_front` does not exist; `insert(begin(), x)` is O(n) because every element must shift right.
explanation.ro: Nu — `vector::push_front` nu exista; `insert(begin(), x)` este O(n) deoarece fiecare element trebuie deplasat la dreapta.

text.en: `deque`
text.ro: `deque`

explanation.en: No — `deque` has cheap `push_front` but does NOT expose `data()`. Its elements live in a directory of non-contiguous chunks.
explanation.ro: Nu — `deque` are `push_front` ieftin dar NU expune `data()`. Elementele sale traiesc intr-un director de bucati ne-contigue.

text.en: `array`
text.ro: `array`

explanation.en: No — `array` is fixed-size; neither `push_front` nor `push_back` exists. It does have `data()` (contiguous storage), but nothing to insert into.
explanation.ro: Nu — `array` are dimensiune fixa; nici `push_front` nici `push_back` nu exista. Are `data()` (stocare contigua), dar nu poti insera in el.

explanation.en: The layout/interface trade-off is a key skill: contiguous → `data()` + cache-friendly traversal but O(n) front insert; chunked → O(1) both ends but no `data()`. Match container to access pattern.
explanation.ro: Compromisul layout/interfata este o abilitate cheie: contiguu → `data()` + parcurgere prietenoasa cu cache-ul, dar inserare frontala O(n); pe bucati → O(1) la ambele capete dar fara `data()`. Potriveste containerul cu tiparul de acces.

question.en: An `std::array<int, 5> a = {1,2,3,4,5};` differs from a C-style `int a[5] = {1,2,3,4,5};` how?
question.ro: Un `std::array<int, 5> a = {1,2,3,4,5};` difera de un tablou C clasic `int a[5] = {1,2,3,4,5};` cum?

text.en: `std::array` is a value-semantic class — it can be passed by value, returned from a function, copied, and exposes `size()`/`begin()`/`end()`. A C array decays to a pointer at function boundary and has no size method.
text.ro: `std::array` este o clasa cu semantica valorica — poate fi transmis prin valoare, returnat dintr-o functie, copiat, si expune `size()`/`begin()`/`end()`. Un tablou C se transforma in pointer la marginea functiei si nu are metoda de dimensiune.

explanation.en: Correct — `std::array` is the modern C++ wrapper that preserves size in the type system and supports STL idioms. C arrays remain raw stack storage with pointer-decay semantics — useful for interop but error-prone in modern C++.
explanation.ro: Corect — `std::array` este wrapper-ul modern C++ care pastreaza dimensiunea in sistemul de tipuri si suporta idiomurile STL. Tablourile C raman stocare bruta pe stiva cu semantica de pointer-decay — utile pentru interoperabilitate, dar predispuse la erori in C++ modern.

text.en: `std::array` stores elements on the heap; a C array stores them on the stack
text.ro: `std::array` stocheaza elementele pe heap; un tablou C le stocheaza pe stiva

explanation.en: No — both live wherever the surrounding object lives. A local `std::array` is on the stack just like a local C array. `std::array` is a thin value-type wrapper, not a heap allocation.
explanation.ro: Nu — ambele traiesc oriunde traieste obiectul inconjurator. Un `std::array` local este pe stiva la fel ca un tablou C local. `std::array` este un wrapper subtire cu semantica valorica, nu o alocare pe heap.

text.en: `std::array` is resizable; a C array is not
text.ro: `std::array` poate fi redimensionat; un tablou C nu

explanation.en: No — `std::array<T, N>` is fixed-size; `N` is part of the type. For a resizable container, use `vector`.
explanation.ro: Nu — `std::array<T, N>` are dimensiune fixa; `N` face parte din tip. Pentru un container redimensionabil, foloseste `vector`.

text.en: They are equivalent — `std::array` is a typedef for the C array
text.ro: Sunt echivalente — `std::array` este un typedef pentru tabloul C

explanation.en: No — `std::array` is a `struct` template with a `T data[N]` member and a member-function interface. The C array is a raw language primitive with no methods.
explanation.ro: Nu — `std::array` este un template de `struct` cu un membru `T data[N]` si o interfata de functii membru. Tabloul C este un primitiv de limbaj brut, fara metode.

explanation.en: Preferring `std::array` over C-style arrays is one of the cheapest modern-C++ wins: size in the type, STL interop, no pointer-decay surprises.
explanation.ro: A prefera `std::array` in detrimentul tablourilor C clasice este una dintre cele mai ieftine castiguri din C++ modern: dimensiune in tip, interop STL, fara surprize de pointer-decay.

question.en: You hold a long sequence and frequently insert/erase elements in the middle. With `vector` this is O(n) per operation because every element after the insertion point must shift. With `deque` it is still O(n) for middle insertions. What data structure achieves O(1) middle insertion — and what does it give up in return?
question.ro: Ai o secventa lunga si inserezi/stergi frecvent elemente la mijloc. Cu `vector` asta este O(n) per operatie deoarece fiecare element de dupa punctul de inserare trebuie deplasat. Cu `deque` ramane O(n) pentru insertii la mijloc. Ce structura de date obtine inserare la mijloc O(1) — si la ce renunta in schimb?

answer.en: A linked list — `std::list` (doubly linked) or `std::forward_list` (singly linked). Insertion at a known position is O(1) (just rewire two pointers; for `forward_list`, one). The trade-off: no random access — `list[i]` and `list.at(i)` do NOT exist. You must walk the list, which is O(n). Iterators lack `+`, `-`, `<` because non-consecutive memory addresses make pointer arithmetic meaningless.
answer.ro: O lista inlantuita — `std::list` (dublu inlantuita) sau `std::forward_list` (simplu inlantuita). Inserarea la o pozitie cunoscuta este O(1) (doar reconectezi doi pointeri; pentru `forward_list`, unul). Compromisul: fara acces aleator — `list[i]` si `list.at(i)` NU exista. Trebuie sa parcurgi lista, ceea ce este O(n). Iteratorii nu au `+`, `-`, `<` deoarece adresele de memorie ne-consecutive fac aritmetica pe pointeri lipsita de sens.

content.en:
**Three traps about `list` and `forward_list`:**
1. *`list` iterators support `it + 5` like vector iterators do.* No — `list` iterators are **bidirectional**, not random-access. They support `++` and `--` only. Arithmetic (`+`, `-`) and comparison (`<`, `>`) are compile errors. Use `std::next(it, 5)` for an explicit O(n) walk.
2. *`forward_list` is just `list` minus `--`.* It also lacks `push_back`, `pop_back`, `size()`, `rbegin()`, and `rend()`. Insertion uses `insert_after()` (not `insert()`), because the iterator points at the predecessor, not at the node itself.
3. *Erasing in a `list` invalidates ALL iterators.* No — `list::erase(it)` invalidates ONLY `it`. Iterators to other nodes remain valid (unlike `vector::erase`, which invalidates `it` and everything after).
content.ro:
**Trei capcane despre `list` si `forward_list`:**
1. *Iteratorii `list` suporta `it + 5` la fel ca iteratorii de vector.* Nu — iteratorii `list` sunt **bidirectionali**, nu cu acces aleator. Suporta doar `++` si `--`. Aritmetica (`+`, `-`) si compararea (`<`, `>`) sunt erori de compilare. Foloseste `std::next(it, 5)` pentru o parcurgere O(n) explicita.
2. *`forward_list` este doar `list` minus `--`.* Lipsesc si `push_back`, `pop_back`, `size()`, `rbegin()` si `rend()`. Inserarea foloseste `insert_after()` (nu `insert()`), pentru ca iteratorul indica predecesorul, nu nodul propriu-zis.
3. *Stergerea intr-un `list` invalideaza TOTI iteratorii.* Nu — `list::erase(it)` invalideaza DOAR `it`. Iteratorii la alte noduri raman valizi (spre deosebire de `vector::erase`, care invalideaza `it` si tot ce este dupa).

content.en:
A `std::list<T>` is a **doubly linked list**: each node holds `T` plus `prev` and `next` pointers. Insertion or deletion at a known position is O(1) — just rewire two pointers. The trade: no `operator[]`, no `at()`. The only access is via iterators or `front()`/`back()`. Iterators are **bidirectional** (`++` and `--` work; `+`, `-`, `<` do NOT).

`std::forward_list<T>` (C++11) is a **singly linked list**: each node holds `T` and just `next`. It is leaner (one pointer per node instead of two) and faster for forward-only traversal, but you cannot go backwards. Its iterators are **forward** (`++` only), and `forward_list` lacks `size()`, `push_back`, `pop_back`, `rbegin`/`rend`. Insertions use `insert_after()` because the iterator names the predecessor.
content.ro:
Un `std::list<T>` este o **lista dublu inlantuita**: fiecare nod tine `T` plus pointerii `prev` si `next`. Inserarea sau stergerea la o pozitie cunoscuta este O(1) — doar reconectezi doi pointeri. Compromis: fara `operator[]`, fara `at()`. Singurul acces este prin iteratori sau `front()`/`back()`. Iteratorii sunt **bidirectionali** (`++` si `--` functioneaza; `+`, `-`, `<` NU).

`std::forward_list<T>` (C++11) este o **lista simplu inlantuita**: fiecare nod tine `T` si doar `next`. Este mai zvelt (un pointer per nod in loc de doi) si mai rapid pentru parcurgere doar inainte, dar nu poti merge inapoi. Iteratorii sunt **inainte** (doar `++`), iar `forward_list` nu are `size()`, `push_back`, `pop_back`, `rbegin`/`rend`. Inserarile folosesc `insert_after()` deoarece iteratorul numeste predecesorul.

content.en: Iterators come in a hierarchy of capabilities. **Random-access** (`vector`, `deque`, `array`) supports `++ -- + - < >`. **Bidirectional** (`list`, `set`, `map`) supports `++ --` only. **Forward** (`forward_list`, `unordered_set`, `unordered_map`) supports `++` only. **Input/Output** (`istream_iterator`, `ostream_iterator`) supports `++` plus read/write but is single-pass. Algorithms in `<algorithm>` are typed by the weakest category they accept; using a stronger iterator is always safe.
content.ro: Iteratorii vin intr-o ierarhie de capacitati. **Acces aleator** (`vector`, `deque`, `array`) suporta `++ -- + - < >`. **Bidirectional** (`list`, `set`, `map`) suporta doar `++ --`. **Inainte** (`forward_list`, `unordered_set`, `unordered_map`) suporta doar `++`. **Input/Output** (`istream_iterator`, `ostream_iterator`) suporta `++` plus citire/scriere dar este single-pass. Algoritmii din `<algorithm>` sunt tipati dupa categoria cea mai slaba pe care o accepta; folosirea unui iterator mai puternic este intotdeauna sigura.

question.en: If `std::list` provides O(1) insertion at any point, why isn't it the default sequence container? Why does the C++ Core Guidelines (and most production code) recommend `std::vector` first?
question.ro: Daca `std::list` ofera inserare O(1) in orice punct, de ce nu este containerul secvential implicit? De ce ghidurile C++ Core Guidelines (si majoritatea codului de productie) recomanda `std::vector` primul?

answer.en: Three reasons. **(1) Cache locality**: `vector`'s contiguous storage means iterating it streams through cache lines linearly — modern CPUs prefetch this for free. `list` chases pointers across the heap, missing cache on almost every step. In practice, iterating a `list` of 1,000,000 ints can be 10-100x slower than iterating a `vector`. **(2) Per-element overhead**: each `list` node stores two extra pointers (16 bytes on x64) plus allocator bookkeeping; a `vector<int>` has zero overhead per element. **(3) Algorithmic O(1) is only useful with an iterator already in hand**: most real workloads start with 'find then insert', and `find` on a `list` is O(n) — wiping out the O(1) advantage. `vector` wins on every common workload except 'splice large sublists between containers'.
answer.ro: Trei motive. **(1) Localitate cache**: stocarea contigua a `vector`-ului inseamna ca iterarea curge prin linii de cache liniar — procesoarele moderne fac prefetch gratuit. `list` urmareste pointeri prin heap, ratand cache-ul aproape la fiecare pas. In practica, iterarea unui `list` de 1.000.000 de intregi poate fi de 10-100x mai lenta decat iterarea unui `vector`. **(2) Overhead pe element**: fiecare nod `list` stocheaza doi pointeri suplimentari (16 octeti pe x64) plus contabilitate de alocator; un `vector<int>` are zero overhead per element. **(3) O(1) algoritmic este util doar cu un iterator deja la indemana**: majoritatea sarcinilor reale incep cu 'cauta apoi insereaza', iar `find` pe un `list` este O(n) — eliminand avantajul O(1). `vector` castiga pe orice sarcina obisnuita, cu exceptia 'splice de sub-liste mari intre containere'.

question.en: You write `list<int>::iterator it = L.begin(); auto five_ahead = it + 5;`. The compiler rejects it. Why?
question.ro: Scrii `list<int>::iterator it = L.begin(); auto five_ahead = it + 5;`. Compilatorul respinge codul. De ce?

text.en: `list` iterators are bidirectional, not random-access — arithmetic (`+`, `-`) is a compile error. Use `std::next(it, 5)` for an explicit O(n) walk.
text.ro: Iteratorii `list` sunt bidirectionali, nu cu acces aleator — aritmetica (`+`, `-`) este eroare de compilare. Foloseste `std::next(it, 5)` pentru o parcurgere O(n) explicita.

explanation.en: Correct — bidirectional iterators only support `++` and `--`. The capability gap is enforced at compile time so the cost of `+ 5` (which on a list is genuinely O(5), not O(1)) is never hidden.
explanation.ro: Corect — iteratorii bidirectionali suporta doar `++` si `--`. Diferenta de capacitate este aplicata la compilare astfel incat costul lui `+ 5` (care pe o lista este intr-adevar O(5), nu O(1)) sa nu fie niciodata ascuns.

text.en: The `+` operator returns an `int` not an iterator
text.ro: Operatorul `+` returneaza un `int`, nu un iterator

explanation.en: No — `list::iterator` simply does not declare `operator+`. The error is 'no such operator', not a wrong return type.
explanation.ro: Nu — `list::iterator` pur si simplu nu declara `operator+`. Eroarea este 'fara astfel de operator', nu un tip de retur gresit.

text.en: `it + 5` only works when `L.size() >= 5`
text.ro: `it + 5` functioneaza doar cand `L.size() >= 5`

explanation.en: No — the operator does not exist regardless of size. It is a static type-system rejection, not a runtime bounds issue.
explanation.ro: Nu — operatorul nu exista, indiferent de dimensiune. Este o respingere statica din partea sistemului de tipuri, nu o problema de limite la runtime.

text.en: `auto` can't deduce the result type of iterator arithmetic
text.ro: `auto` nu poate deduce tipul rezultatului din aritmetica pe iteratori

explanation.en: No — `auto` works fine when there is something to deduce. The error is that the expression has no valid type at all.
explanation.ro: Nu — `auto` functioneaza bine cand exista ceva de dedus. Eroarea este ca expresia nu are deloc un tip valid.

explanation.en: The iterator-category system makes data structure costs visible: if `+` is not callable, you can't pretend an O(n) walk is O(1). It is a deliberate type-system gate, not an oversight.
explanation.ro: Sistemul de categorii de iteratori face vizibile costurile structurilor de date: daca `+` nu este apelabil, nu poti pretinde ca o parcurgere O(n) este O(1). Este o poarta deliberata din sistemul de tipuri, nu o omisiune.

question.en: Which method does `std::forward_list` LACK that all four other sequence containers (`vector`, `deque`, `array`, `list`) provide?
question.ro: Ce metoda LIPSESTE din `std::forward_list` pe care celelalte patru containere secventiale (`vector`, `deque`, `array`, `list`) o ofera?

text.en: Reverse iterators (`rbegin()` / `rend()`) — a singly linked list has no `prev` pointer, so reverse traversal is not O(n) reachable
text.ro: Iteratori inversi (`rbegin()` / `rend()`) — o lista simplu inlantuita nu are pointer `prev`, deci parcurgerea inversa nu este O(n) accesibila

explanation.en: Correct — `forward_list` nodes have only a `next` pointer; constructing a `reverse_iterator` would require either an extra backwards traversal each step or a doubled storage cost. Both defeat the purpose of `forward_list` being lean.
explanation.ro: Corect — nodurile `forward_list` au doar un pointer `next`; construirea unui `reverse_iterator` ar necesita fie o parcurgere inversa la fiecare pas, fie un cost dublu de stocare. Ambele anuleaza scopul `forward_list` de a fi zvelt.

text.en: `front()`
text.ro: `front()`

explanation.en: No — `forward_list` does expose `front()`. What it lacks is `back()` (no tail pointer) and `push_back` / `pop_back`.
explanation.ro: Nu — `forward_list` expune `front()`. Ii lipseste `back()` (fara pointer la coada) si `push_back` / `pop_back`.

text.en: Forward iteration via `begin()` / `end()`
text.ro: Iterare inainte via `begin()` / `end()`

explanation.en: No — forward iteration is the whole point. `begin()` / `end()` are present; the missing direction is REVERSE iteration.
explanation.ro: Nu — iterarea inainte este chiar scopul. `begin()` / `end()` sunt prezente; directia care lipseste este iterarea INAPOI.

text.en: `clear()`
text.ro: `clear()`

explanation.en: No — `forward_list::clear()` exists and drops every node.
explanation.ro: Nu — `forward_list::clear()` exista si elimina fiecare nod.

explanation.en: Reverse iterators are the canonical capability gap that distinguishes singly linked from every other sequence container. The compiler enforces it at the type level.
explanation.ro: Iteratorii inversi sunt diferenta canonica de capacitate care distinge o lista simplu inlantuita de orice alt container secvential. Compilatorul aplica regula la nivel de tip.

question.en: You want a LIFO **stack** of integers. You could write your own class wrapping `vector<int>` with `push`, `pop`, `top`. Or you could ask the STL for one. The STL ships `std::stack`, `std::queue`, and `std::priority_queue` — but none of them is a 'container' in the same sense as `vector`. What is the relationship?
question.ro: Vrei o **stiva** LIFO de intregi. Ai putea scrie propria clasa care impacheteaza `vector<int>` cu `push`, `pop`, `top`. Sau poti cere STL-ului una. STL-ul vine cu `std::stack`, `std::queue` si `std::priority_queue` — dar niciuna dintre ele nu este 'container' in acelasi sens ca `vector`. Care este relatia?

answer.en: They are **container adaptors**: thin wrappers that take an existing sequence container as a template parameter (e.g., `stack<int, deque<int>>`) and expose a narrowed interface (`push`, `pop`, `top`/`front` only). The adaptor has no iterators, no `operator[]`, no traversal — just the LIFO/FIFO/priority discipline. The default underlying container is `deque` for `stack` and `queue`, `vector` for `priority_queue`.
answer.ro: Sunt **adaptori de container**: invelisuri subtiri care iau un container secvential existent ca parametru template (de ex. `stack<int, deque<int>>`) si expun o interfata restransa (`push`, `pop`, `top`/`front` doar). Adaptorul nu are iteratori, nu are `operator[]`, nu are parcurgere — doar disciplina LIFO/FIFO/prioritate. Containerul implicit este `deque` pentru `stack` si `queue`, `vector` pentru `priority_queue`.

content.en:
**Three traps about adaptors:**
1. *Any sequence container can underlie any adaptor.* No — there are hard compatibility constraints. **`queue<T, vector<T>>`** is a COMPILE error: `queue` needs `pop_front`, which `vector` lacks. **`priority_queue<T, list<T>>`** is a COMPILE error: `priority_queue` needs random access (it uses heap operations), which `list` does not provide.
2. *Adaptors expose iterators, just like containers.* No — `stack`, `queue`, `priority_queue` have NO `begin()`, NO `end()`, NO `operator[]`. The only access is via `top()`/`front()`+`back()` and `pop()`. Iterating an adaptor requires popping every element (destructive) or reaching into the underlying container (non-standard via `_Get_container()`).
3. *`priority_queue<int>` extracts the SMALLEST element first.* No — by default it is a **max-heap**: `top()` returns the LARGEST element. For min-heap behaviour, pass `std::greater<int>` as the third template argument.
content.ro:
**Trei capcane despre adaptori:**
1. *Orice container secvential poate sta sub orice adaptor.* Nu — exista constrangeri dure de compatibilitate. **`queue<T, vector<T>>`** este eroare la COMPILARE: `queue` are nevoie de `pop_front`, pe care `vector` nu il are. **`priority_queue<T, list<T>>`** este eroare la COMPILARE: `priority_queue` are nevoie de acces aleator (foloseste operatii de heap), pe care `list` nu il ofera.
2. *Adaptorii expun iteratori, ca si containerele.* Nu — `stack`, `queue`, `priority_queue` NU au `begin()`, NU au `end()`, NU au `operator[]`. Singurul acces este prin `top()`/`front()`+`back()` si `pop()`. Iterarea unui adaptor cere fie scoaterea fiecarui element (distructiva), fie patrunderea in containerul intern (non-standard prin `_Get_container()`).
3. *`priority_queue<int>` extrage cel mai MIC element primul.* Nu — implicit este un **max-heap**: `top()` returneaza cel mai MARE element. Pentru min-heap, transmite `std::greater<int>` ca al treilea argument template.

content.en:
Three adaptors share the same wrapping idea but differ in their access discipline:
- **`stack<T, Container = deque<T>>`** — LIFO. Methods: `push`, `pop`, `top`, `empty`, `size`. The compatible underlying containers are `vector`, `deque`, `list` — anything with `push_back` and `pop_back`.
- **`queue<T, Container = deque<T>>`** — FIFO. Methods: `push`, `pop`, `front`, `back`, `empty`, `size`. The compatible underlying containers are `deque` and `list` — needs `push_back` AND `pop_front`. `vector` is OUT (no `pop_front`).
- **`priority_queue<T, Container = vector<T>, Compare = less<T>>`** — sorted extraction. Methods: `push`, `pop`, `top`, `empty`, `size`. The compatible underlying containers are `vector` and `deque` — needs random access for heap operations. `list` is OUT. By default it is a max-heap; pass `std::greater<T>` for a min-heap.
content.ro:
Trei adaptori impart aceeasi idee de impachetare, dar difera prin disciplina de acces:
- **`stack<T, Container = deque<T>>`** — LIFO. Metode: `push`, `pop`, `top`, `empty`, `size`. Containerele interne compatibile sunt `vector`, `deque`, `list` — orice are `push_back` si `pop_back`.
- **`queue<T, Container = deque<T>>`** — FIFO. Metode: `push`, `pop`, `front`, `back`, `empty`, `size`. Containerele interne compatibile sunt `deque` si `list` — au nevoie de `push_back` SI `pop_front`. `vector` este EXCLUS (nu are `pop_front`).
- **`priority_queue<T, Container = vector<T>, Compare = less<T>>`** — extragere sortata. Metode: `push`, `pop`, `top`, `empty`, `size`. Containerele interne compatibile sunt `vector` si `deque` — au nevoie de acces aleator pentru operatii de heap. `list` este EXCLUS. Implicit este max-heap; transmite `std::greater<T>` pentru un min-heap.

content.en: A class template that takes an existing sequence container as a template parameter and re-exposes its operations under a restricted interface. The adaptor has no iterators of its own; it just enforces the access discipline (LIFO / FIFO / priority) on top of the wrapped container. The MSVC-specific method `_Get_container()` returns a reference to the underlying container — useful for debugging or extending the adaptor, but non-standard.
content.ro: Un template de clasa care ia un container secvential existent ca parametru template si reexpune operatiile sale sub o interfata restransa. Adaptorul nu are iteratori proprii; doar aplica disciplina de acces (LIFO / FIFO / prioritate) peste containerul invelit. Metoda specifica MSVC `_Get_container()` returneaza o referinta la containerul intern — utila pentru debugging sau extinderea adaptorului, dar nestandard.

question.en: Why does `priority_queue<T, list<T>>` fail to compile, while `stack<T, list<T>>` works fine?
question.ro: De ce `priority_queue<T, list<T>>` esueaza la compilare, in timp ce `stack<T, list<T>>` functioneaza fara probleme?

answer.en: `priority_queue` is implemented on top of a **binary heap**, which needs random access — heap operations index into the array (`a[parent(i)]`, `a[child(i)]`) and `swap` arbitrary positions in O(1). A `list` cannot do that; reaching position `i` is O(i). `stack` has no such need: `push` is `push_back` and `pop` is `pop_back` — both O(1) on any sequence container that provides them, including `list`. The compatibility table is not arbitrary; it tracks the algorithms the adaptor secretly runs.
answer.ro: `priority_queue` este implementat peste un **heap binar**, care are nevoie de acces aleator — operatiile de heap indexeaza in tablou (`a[parent(i)]`, `a[child(i)]`) si fac `swap` pe pozitii arbitrare in O(1). Un `list` nu poate face asta; accesarea pozitiei `i` este O(i). `stack` nu are aceasta nevoie: `push` este `push_back` si `pop` este `pop_back` — ambele O(1) pe orice container secvential care le ofera, inclusiv `list`. Tabelul de compatibilitate nu este arbitrar; reflecta algoritmii pe care adaptorul ii ruleaza in spate.

question.en: Why is `std::queue<int, std::vector<int>>` a compile error?
question.ro: De ce `std::queue<int, std::vector<int>>` este eroare de compilare?

text.en: `queue` requires `pop_front` from its underlying container, and `vector` does not provide it
text.ro: `queue` cere `pop_front` din containerul intern, iar `vector` nu il ofera

explanation.en: Correct — `queue::pop` is implemented as `c.pop_front()`. `vector` would need O(n) shifting for `pop_front` (it doesn't provide the method at all), so the standard forbids the combination at compile time via the adaptor's member-function requirements.
explanation.ro: Corect — `queue::pop` este implementat ca `c.pop_front()`. `vector` ar avea nevoie de deplasare O(n) pentru `pop_front` (nici nu ofera metoda), deci standardul interzice combinatia la compilare prin cerintele de functii membru ale adaptorului.

text.en: `queue` requires bidirectional iterators, and `vector` only provides random-access
text.ro: `queue` cere iteratori bidirectionali, iar `vector` ofera doar acces aleator

explanation.en: No — random-access is a stronger category than bidirectional. The compatibility issue is `pop_front`, not iterator categories.
explanation.ro: Nu — accesul aleator este o categorie mai puternica decat bidirectional. Problema de compatibilitate este `pop_front`, nu categoriile de iteratori.

text.en: `vector` is single-threaded but `queue` requires thread safety
text.ro: `vector` este monofir, dar `queue` cere siguranta firelor

explanation.en: No — neither STL containers nor adaptors offer thread safety. The error is structural: missing member function.
explanation.ro: Nu — nici containerele STL, nici adaptorii nu ofera siguranta firelor. Eroarea este structurala: lipseste o functie membru.

text.en: `vector<int>` is not a valid template argument for any adaptor
text.ro: `vector<int>` nu este argument template valid pentru niciun adaptor

explanation.en: No — `vector<int>` is the DEFAULT underlying container for `priority_queue`, and it is acceptable for `stack`. It is rejected only for `queue` because of `pop_front`.
explanation.ro: Nu — `vector<int>` este containerul intern IMPLICIT pentru `priority_queue` si este acceptabil pentru `stack`. Este respins doar pentru `queue` din cauza lui `pop_front`.

explanation.en: The compatibility table is enforced by the adaptor's reliance on specific member functions of the underlying container. Mismatches are caught at instantiation time, not at runtime.
explanation.ro: Tabelul de compatibilitate este aplicat prin dependenta adaptorului de functii membru specifice ale containerului intern. Nepotrivirile sunt prinse la momentul instantierii, nu la runtime.

question.en: What does `pq.top()` return for `std::priority_queue<int> pq; pq.push(3); pq.push(7); pq.push(1);`?
question.ro: Ce returneaza `pq.top()` pentru `std::priority_queue<int> pq; pq.push(3); pq.push(7); pq.push(1);`?

text.en: `7` — `priority_queue<int>` is a MAX-heap by default; `top()` returns the largest element
text.ro: `7` — `priority_queue<int>` este implicit un MAX-heap; `top()` returneaza cel mai mare element

explanation.en: Correct — the default comparator is `std::less<T>`, which orders elements so that the LARGEST sits at the top of the heap. For a min-heap, instantiate as `priority_queue<int, vector<int>, std::greater<int>>`.
explanation.ro: Corect — comparatorul implicit este `std::less<T>`, care ordoneaza elementele astfel incat cel mai MARE sa stea in varful heap-ului. Pentru un min-heap, instantiaza ca `priority_queue<int, vector<int>, std::greater<int>>`.

text.en: `1` — `priority_queue` extracts the smallest first (min-heap by default)
text.ro: `1` — `priority_queue` extrage cel mai mic primul (min-heap implicit)

explanation.en: No — the C++ default is max-heap. This catches many students used to other languages (Python `heapq` is min-heap by default).
explanation.ro: Nu — implicitul C++ este max-heap. Aceasta capcana ii prinde pe multi studenti obisnuiti cu alte limbaje (Python `heapq` este min-heap implicit).

text.en: `3` — the first element pushed (FIFO order)
text.ro: `3` — primul element adaugat (ordine FIFO)

explanation.en: No — `priority_queue` does not follow insertion order. It orders by priority via the comparator (default `less` → max at top).
explanation.ro: Nu — `priority_queue` nu urmeaza ordinea inserarii. Ordoneaza dupa prioritate prin comparator (implicit `less` → maximul in varf).

text.en: `1` — `priority_queue` follows LIFO order like `stack`
text.ro: `1` — `priority_queue` urmeaza ordinea LIFO ca `stack`

explanation.en: No — `priority_queue` is heap-ordered, not LIFO. The most recently pushed element is not generally at the top unless it happens to be the largest.
explanation.ro: Nu — `priority_queue` este ordonat ca heap, nu LIFO. Cel mai recent adaugat element nu este in general in varf, decat daca se intampla sa fie cel mai mare.

explanation.en: Max-heap default is the most common C++ surprise for students with Python or Java priority-queue experience. Always check the comparator when porting between languages.
explanation.ro: Implicitul max-heap este cea mai frecventa surpriza C++ pentru studentii cu experienta de coada cu prioritate in Python sau Java. Verifica intotdeauna comparatorul cand portezi intre limbaje.

question.en: You want to write the same `printf`-style formatting code regardless of whether the destination is the console, a file, or an in-memory buffer. The C function `fprintf` already handles files, but it does not work for an in-memory string, and `sprintf` does not work for the console. C++ unifies these. What is the abstraction it uses?
question.ro: Vrei sa scrii acelasi cod de formatare in stil `printf` indiferent daca destinatia este consola, un fisier sau un buffer in memorie. Functia C `fprintf` se ocupa deja de fisiere, dar nu functioneaza pentru un sir in memorie, iar `sprintf` nu functioneaza pentru consola. C++ unifica acestea. Care este abstractizarea folosita?

answer.en: The **iostream hierarchy**: an inheritance tree rooted at `ios_base`, whose concrete leaves (`cout`, `cerr`, `ofstream`, `ostringstream`) share the same `operator<<` interface. The same `out << x << y << z` line works on any `ostream`. Symmetrically `cin`, `ifstream`, `istringstream` share `operator>>`. The class hierarchy is the mechanism through which polymorphism delivers 'write to anywhere' as one interface.
answer.ro: **Ierarhia iostream**: un arbore de mostenire cu radacina `ios_base`, ale carui frunze concrete (`cout`, `cerr`, `ofstream`, `ostringstream`) impart aceeasi interfata `operator<<`. Aceeasi linie `out << x << y << z` functioneaza pe orice `ostream`. Simetric, `cin`, `ifstream`, `istringstream` impart `operator>>`. Ierarhia de clase este mecanismul prin care polimorfismul ofera 'scrie oriunde' ca o singura interfata.

content.en:
**Three traps about I/O streams:**
1. *`endl` is equivalent to `"
"`.* No — `endl` writes the newline AND **flushes** the stream. In a tight loop, repeated `endl` is dramatically slower than `"
"`. Use `"
"` unless you need an immediate flush.
2. *Reading a binary file with text-mode `>>` works.* No — text mode performs line-ending translation (`
` → `
` on Windows) and may stop at whitespace. For raw bytes, open with `std::ios::binary` and use `read()` / `write()`.
3. *`if (stream)` after `>>` only tests for end-of-file.* No — it tests the combined `failbit` and `badbit`. A failed conversion (e.g., reading `"abc"` into an `int`) sets `failbit` and leaves the stream in a bad state until you `clear()` it.
content.ro:
**Trei capcane despre fluxurile I/O:**
1. *`endl` este echivalent cu `"
"`.* Nu — `endl` scrie newline-ul SI face **flush** la flux. Intr-o bucla stransa, `endl` repetat este mult mai lent decat `"
"`. Foloseste `"
"` decat daca ai nevoie de un flush imediat.
2. *Citirea unui fisier binar cu `>>` in mod text functioneaza.* Nu — modul text face traducere de terminatori de linie (`
` → `
` pe Windows) si se poate opri la spatii albe. Pentru octeti bruti, deschide cu `std::ios::binary` si foloseste `read()` / `write()`.
3. *`if (stream)` dupa `>>` testeaza doar end-of-file.* Nu — testeaza combinat `failbit` si `badbit`. O conversie esuata (de ex. citirea `"abc"` intr-un `int`) seteaza `failbit` si lasa fluxul intr-o stare proasta pana cand apelezi `clear()`.

content.en:
The C++ stream hierarchy has four base layers:
- **`ios_base`** — locale, flags (`hex`, `dec`, `boolalpha`, ...), state bits (`good`, `eof`, `fail`, `bad`). No I/O methods.
- **`ios`** — buffer + character traits. Still abstract.
- **`istream`** — adds `operator>>`, `get()`, `getline()`, `read()`, `seekg()`, `tellg()`.
- **`ostream`** — adds `operator<<`, `put()`, `write()`, `seekp()`, `tellp()`.

The concrete leaves are:
- **`istream` side**: `cin` (stdin), `ifstream` (file input), `istringstream` (in-memory input).
- **`ostream` side**: `cout` (stdout), `cerr` (stderr unbuffered), `clog` (stderr buffered), `ofstream`, `ostringstream`.
- **Both sides (multiple inheritance from `istream` + `ostream` via `iostream`)**: `fstream` (file in+out), `stringstream` (in-memory in+out).
content.ro:
Ierarhia fluxurilor C++ are patru straturi de baza:
- **`ios_base`** — locale, flag-uri (`hex`, `dec`, `boolalpha`, ...), biti de stare (`good`, `eof`, `fail`, `bad`). Fara metode I/O.
- **`ios`** — buffer + trasaturi de caractere. Inca abstract.
- **`istream`** — adauga `operator>>`, `get()`, `getline()`, `read()`, `seekg()`, `tellg()`.
- **`ostream`** — adauga `operator<<`, `put()`, `write()`, `seekp()`, `tellp()`.

Frunzele concrete sunt:
- **Partea `istream`**: `cin` (stdin), `ifstream` (intrare din fisier), `istringstream` (intrare din memorie).
- **Partea `ostream`**: `cout` (stdout), `cerr` (stderr nebufferat), `clog` (stderr bufferat), `ofstream`, `ostringstream`.
- **Ambele parti (mostenire multipla din `istream` + `ostream` via `iostream`)**: `fstream` (fisier in+out), `stringstream` (memorie in+out).

items.en: The virtual inheritance of `ios` solves the diamond problem so each `fstream` / `stringstream` has ONE `ios_base` subobject, not two.
items.ro: Mostenirea virtuala a `ios` rezolva problema diamantului astfel incat fiecare `fstream` / `stringstream` are UN singur subobiect `ios_base`, nu doua.

content.en: A value passed to a stream via `<<` (or `>>`) that mutates the stream's formatting state rather than writing characters. Examples: `std::endl` (writes `'\n'` and flushes), `std::hex` / `std::dec` / `std::oct` (change integer base), `std::boolalpha` (prints booleans as `true`/`false`, not `1`/`0`), `std::setprecision(n)` (decimal digits for floating-point output), `std::setw(n)` (next-field width). Implemented as function pointers or simple structs the stream knows how to interpret.
content.ro: O valoare transmisa unui flux prin `<<` (sau `>>`) care modifica starea de formatare a fluxului, nu scrie caractere. Exemple: `std::endl` (scrie `'\n'` si face flush), `std::hex` / `std::dec` / `std::oct` (schimba baza intregilor), `std::boolalpha` (afiseaza boolean-i ca `true`/`false`, nu `1`/`0`), `std::setprecision(n)` (cifre zecimale pentru iesirea cu virgula mobila), `std::setw(n)` (latimea urmatorului camp). Implementati ca pointeri de functii sau structuri simple pe care fluxul stie sa le interpreteze.

rows.en: Writes `'\n'` AND flushes the stream. Slower than `"\n"` in hot loops.
rows.ro: Scrie `'\n'` SI face flush. Mai lent decat `"\n"` in bucle stranse.

rows.en: Sets the integer base for subsequent `<<`/`>>` to 10, 16, 8.
rows.ro: Seteaza baza intregilor pentru `<<`/`>>` urmatoare la 10, 16, 8.

rows.en: Sets decimal precision for floating-point output. Persistent until changed.
rows.ro: Seteaza precizia zecimala pentru iesirea cu virgula mobila. Persistenta pana la schimbare.

rows.en: Minimum field width for the NEXT output operation only (not sticky).
rows.ro: Latimea minima a campului pentru URMATOAREA operatie de iesire doar (nu este persistenta).

question.en: An `fstream` inherits from both `istream` AND `ostream` (via `iostream`). Both base classes inherit from `ios`. Without virtual inheritance, `fstream` would have TWO copies of every `ios` member — including the buffer and state flags. What standard C++ mechanism prevents this duplication?
question.ro: Un `fstream` mosteneste atat din `istream` CAT SI din `ostream` (via `iostream`). Ambele clase de baza mostenesc din `ios`. Fara mostenire virtuala, `fstream` ar avea DOUA copii ale fiecarui membru `ios` — inclusiv buffer-ul si flag-urile de stare. Ce mecanism standard C++ previne aceasta duplicare?

answer.en: **Virtual inheritance** of `ios` by both `istream` and `ostream`. Both declare `class istream : virtual public ios` (and similarly for `ostream`). The compiler ensures that any class deriving from both — like `iostream` and its children `fstream` and `stringstream` — has only ONE shared `ios` subobject. This is the canonical textbook example of the diamond problem and its standard library solution.
answer.ro: **Mostenirea virtuala** a `ios` de catre `istream` si `ostream`. Ambele declara `class istream : virtual public ios` (si la fel pentru `ostream`). Compilatorul se asigura ca orice clasa derivata din ambele — ca `iostream` si copiii sai `fstream` si `stringstream` — are doar UN subobiect `ios` partajat. Acesta este exemplul canonic de manual al problemei diamantului si al solutiei standard din biblioteca.

question.en: In a hot loop writing 1,000,000 integers to a file, `out << i << endl;` and `out << i << "\n";` differ how?
question.ro: Intr-o bucla stransa care scrie 1.000.000 de intregi intr-un fisier, `out << i << endl;` si `out << i << "\n";` difera cum?

text.en: `endl` writes `\n` AND flushes the stream after every iteration; `"\n"` writes only the character. The flush version is dramatically slower because each flush is a syscall.
text.ro: `endl` scrie `\n` SI face flush la flux dupa fiecare iteratie; `"\n"` scrie doar caracterul. Versiunea cu flush este mult mai lenta deoarece fiecare flush este un syscall.

explanation.en: Correct — the flush forces the stream buffer to commit to the OS, costing a syscall per iteration. In a million-iteration loop the gap is typically 10-100x. Use `"\n"` and `flush` explicitly only when you need on-disk durability.
explanation.ro: Corect — flush-ul forteaza buffer-ul fluxului sa transmita la OS, costand un syscall per iteratie. Intr-o bucla de un milion, diferenta este de obicei 10-100x. Foloseste `"\n"` si `flush` explicit doar cand ai nevoie de persistenta pe disc.

text.en: They are identical — `endl` is a macro that expands to `"\n"`
text.ro: Sunt identice — `endl` este un macro care se expandeaza la `"\n"`

explanation.en: No — `endl` is a manipulator that writes `'\n'` AND calls `flush()` on the stream. It is a function, not a macro.
explanation.ro: Nu — `endl` este un manipulator care scrie `'\n'` SI apeleaza `flush()` pe flux. Este o functie, nu un macro.

text.en: `"\n"` writes nothing on Windows because of line-ending translation
text.ro: `"\n"` nu scrie nimic pe Windows din cauza traducerii terminatorilor de linie

explanation.en: No — `"\n"` writes a newline character. On Windows in text mode the runtime translates it to `\r\n` on disk, but the byte IS written. It writes nothing only when the stream is in a fail state.
explanation.ro: Nu — `"\n"` scrie un caracter newline. Pe Windows in mod text, runtime-ul il traduce in `\r\n` pe disc, dar octetul ESTE scris. Nu scrie nimic doar cand fluxul este in stare de esec.

text.en: `endl` is type-safe but `"\n"` is not
text.ro: `endl` este sigur de tip, dar `"\n"` nu

explanation.en: No — both are type-safe via `operator<<` overloads. The relevant difference is FLUSH behaviour, not type safety.
explanation.ro: Nu — ambele sunt sigure de tip prin supraincarcarile `operator<<`. Diferenta relevanta este comportamentul de FLUSH, nu siguranta tipurilor.

explanation.en: The `endl`-vs-`"\n"` performance gap is one of the cheapest wins in any C++ logging code. The flush only matters when you need crash-safe persistence.
explanation.ro: Diferenta de performanta `endl` vs `"\n"` este unul dintre cele mai ieftine castiguri in orice cod C++ de logare. Flush-ul conteaza doar cand ai nevoie de persistenta dupa crash.

question.en: You want to read raw bytes (not text) from a file. Which combination of header, stream type, and mode flag is correct?
question.ro: Vrei sa citesti octeti bruti (nu text) dintr-un fisier. Care combinatie de header, tip de flux si flag de mod este corecta?

text.en: `<fstream>` + `std::ifstream` opened with `std::ios::binary`, then use `read()` / `gcount()`
text.ro: `<fstream>` + `std::ifstream` deschis cu `std::ios::binary`, apoi foloseste `read()` / `gcount()`

explanation.en: Correct — `ios::binary` disables line-ending translation and lets `read()` consume raw bytes. `gcount()` returns how many bytes were actually read. `operator>>` with text-mode would mangle binary data on Windows.
explanation.ro: Corect — `ios::binary` dezactiveaza traducerea terminatorilor de linie si permite `read()` sa consume octeti bruti. `gcount()` returneaza cati octeti au fost cititi efectiv. `operator>>` in mod text ar strica datele binare pe Windows.

text.en: `<iostream>` + `std::cin` with `>>` — `cin` handles binary input by default
text.ro: `<iostream>` + `std::cin` cu `>>` — `cin` se ocupa de intrarea binara implicit

explanation.en: No — `cin` is a text-mode console stream. Reading via `>>` skips whitespace and would split binary data at byte boundaries that happen to be whitespace.
explanation.ro: Nu — `cin` este un flux de consola in mod text. Citirea via `>>` sare peste spatii albe si ar imparti datele binare la marginile de octeti care se intampla sa fie spatii.

text.en: `<fstream>` + `std::ifstream` in default (text) mode with `getline` — handles binary fine
text.ro: `<fstream>` + `std::ifstream` in mod implicit (text) cu `getline` — gestioneaza binarul corect

explanation.en: No — text mode translates `\r\n` to `\n` on Windows, corrupting binary data. `getline` also stops at any newline byte in the binary stream.
explanation.ro: Nu — modul text traduce `\r\n` in `\n` pe Windows, corupand datele binare. `getline` se opreste si la orice octet de newline din fluxul binar.

text.en: `<sstream>` + `std::istringstream` — works equally well for files and memory
text.ro: `<sstream>` + `std::istringstream` — functioneaza la fel de bine pentru fisiere si memorie

explanation.en: No — `istringstream` reads from an in-memory string, not a file. You would first need to load the file into a string, which defeats the purpose.
explanation.ro: Nu — `istringstream` citeste dintr-un sir in memorie, nu dintr-un fisier. Ar trebui mai intai sa incarci fisierul intr-un sir, ceea ce anuleaza scopul.

explanation.en: Binary mode is a one-line discipline: pass `ios::binary` at open time and use `read`/`write`/`gcount`. Forgetting it on Windows is a classic 'works on my Linux machine' bug.
explanation.ro: Modul binar este o disciplina de o linie: transmite `ios::binary` la deschidere si foloseste `read`/`write`/`gcount`. Uitarea pe Windows este un bug clasic de 'merge pe Linux-ul meu'.

question.en: C strings (`char*`) leak ownership questions all over the codebase: who allocates? who frees? what if it isn't null-terminated? what if it holds UTF-16? C++ wraps this in `std::string` — but `std::string` is itself a typedef of something more general. What is the actual template, and why is it generic?
question.ro: Sirurile C (`char*`) imprastie intrebari de proprietate prin tot codul: cine aloca? cine elibereaza? ce daca nu este null-terminat? ce daca tine UTF-16? C++ impacheteaza asta in `std::string` — dar `std::string` insusi este un typedef pentru ceva mai general. Care este template-ul real si de ce este generic?

answer.en: `std::basic_string<CharT, Traits, Allocator>`. `std::string` is `basic_string<char>`; `std::wstring` is `basic_string<wchar_t>`; `std::u16string` (C++11) is `basic_string<char16_t>` and `std::u32string` is `basic_string<char32_t>`. The template is generic so the same code path handles 8-bit ASCII, 16-bit UTF-16, and 32-bit UTF-32. The `Traits` parameter (`char_traits<CharT>`) hosts the character operations (compare, copy, length); specializations use `memcpy`/`memcmp` for `char` for speed.
answer.ro: `std::basic_string<CharT, Traits, Allocator>`. `std::string` este `basic_string<char>`; `std::wstring` este `basic_string<wchar_t>`; `std::u16string` (C++11) este `basic_string<char16_t>` iar `std::u32string` este `basic_string<char32_t>`. Template-ul este generic astfel incat aceeasi cale de cod sa gestioneze ASCII pe 8 biti, UTF-16 pe 16 biti si UTF-32 pe 32 de biti. Parametrul `Traits` (`char_traits<CharT>`) gazduieste operatiile pe caractere (compare, copy, length); specializarile folosesc `memcpy`/`memcmp` pentru `char` pentru viteza.

content.en:
**Three traps about strings:**
1. *`std::string_view::data()` returns a null-terminated C string.* NO. `string_view` is a view over a (pointer, length) pair — it makes NO guarantee about the byte past the end. Passing `sv.data()` to `printf("%s", ...)` is **undefined behaviour** unless you have separately verified null-termination.
2. *`string s2(s1 + " go ");` constructs `s2` directly from the concatenation.* True, but note that `s1 + " go "` allocates a TEMPORARY `string`. For one-off concatenation that is fine; in a hot loop, use `+=` or `s.append(...)` to reuse the existing buffer.
3. *`char_traits<wchar_t>::length(p)` walks the array until a 0 word.* True, but the cost is O(n) where `n` is the wide-character length — NOT the byte length. A 1000-wchar string scans 1000 wide-character positions. Cache and prefetch behaviour differ from `strlen` on plain `char*`.
content.ro:
**Trei capcane despre siruri:**
1. *`std::string_view::data()` returneaza un sir C null-terminat.* NU. `string_view` este o vedere peste o pereche (pointer, lungime) — NU ofera nicio garantie despre octetul de dupa final. Transmiterea `sv.data()` catre `printf("%s", ...)` este **comportament nedefinit** decat daca ai verificat separat null-terminarea.
2. *`string s2(s1 + " go ");` construieste `s2` direct din concatenare.* Adevarat, dar nota ca `s1 + " go "` aloca un `string` TEMPORAR. Pentru concatenare punctuala este in regula; intr-o bucla stransa, foloseste `+=` sau `s.append(...)` pentru a refolosi buffer-ul existent.
3. *`char_traits<wchar_t>::length(p)` parcurge tabloul pana la un cuvant 0.* Adevarat, dar costul este O(n) unde `n` este lungimea in caractere late — NU lungimea in octeti. Un sir de 1000 de wchar parcurge 1000 de pozitii. Cache-ul si pre-incarcarea se comporta diferit fata de `strlen` pe `char*` clasic.

content.en:
**`basic_string<CharT, Traits, Allocator>`** is the generic owning string. `Traits` is typically `char_traits<CharT>` — a static class providing primitive operations (`eq`, `lt`, `length`, `assign`, `compare`, `find`, `move`, `copy`). The specialization for `char` calls `memcpy`/`memcmp`; for other character types the operations work char-by-char.

**Construction patterns** mirror most data structures: copy of another string, substring (offset + length), repeated character, concatenation, range from iterators.

**`std::string_view` (C++17)** is a NON-OWNING view: a `const CharT*` plus a `size_t` length. It is **cheap to pass by value** (16 bytes on x64). Use it for read-only parameters where the caller already owns the string. The lifetime contract is the caller's responsibility — a `string_view` outliving its source is dangling.
content.ro:
**`basic_string<CharT, Traits, Allocator>`** este sirul generic care detine memoria. `Traits` este de obicei `char_traits<CharT>` — o clasa statica ce ofera operatii primitive (`eq`, `lt`, `length`, `assign`, `compare`, `find`, `move`, `copy`). Specializarea pentru `char` apeleaza `memcpy`/`memcmp`; pentru alte tipuri de caractere, operatiile lucreaza caracter cu caracter.

**Tipare de constructie** reflecta majoritatea structurilor de date: copie a altui sir, subsir (offset + lungime), caracter repetat, concatenare, interval din iteratori.

**`std::string_view` (C++17)** este o vedere NE-PROPRIETARA: un `const CharT*` plus o lungime `size_t`. Este **ieftin de transmis prin valoare** (16 octeti pe x64). Foloseste-l pentru parametri de doar-citire unde apelantul detine deja sirul. Contractul de durata de viata este responsabilitatea apelantului — un `string_view` care supravietuieste sursei sale este dangling.

content.en: Static class template providing the primitive operations that `basic_string` (and the streams) need on individual characters: `eq(a,b)`, `lt(a,b)`, `length(p)`, `assign(a,b)`, `compare(p,q,n)`, `find(p,n,a)`, `move(d,s,n)`, `copy(d,s,n)`. The default specializations for `char` and `wchar_t` are tuned via `memcpy`/`memcmp`/`memchr`; user-defined `CharT` types must supply their own specialization for `basic_string<CharT>` to work.
content.ro: Template static de clasa care ofera operatiile primitive pe care `basic_string` (si fluxurile) le cer pe caractere individuale: `eq(a,b)`, `lt(a,b)`, `length(p)`, `assign(a,b)`, `compare(p,q,n)`, `find(p,n,a)`, `move(d,s,n)`, `copy(d,s,n)`. Specializarile implicite pentru `char` si `wchar_t` sunt optimizate prin `memcpy`/`memcmp`/`memchr`; tipurile `CharT` definite de utilizator trebuie sa furnizeze propria specializare pentru ca `basic_string<CharT>` sa functioneze.

question.en: You write a function `void print(std::string_view sv)` and call it as `print("hello")` from `main`. Why does the standard library author tell you to prefer this signature over `void print(const std::string& s)`?
question.ro: Scrii o functie `void print(std::string_view sv)` si o apelezi ca `print("hello")` din `main`. De ce autorul bibliotecii standard iti spune sa preferi aceasta semnatura in locul `void print(const std::string& s)`?

answer.en: Three reasons. **(1) No allocation** for the string literal: `const std::string&` would force the compiler to construct a temporary `std::string("hello")`, which allocates and copies 5 bytes plus null terminator. `string_view` just wraps the literal pointer + length — zero allocation. **(2) Caller-owns-buffer flexibility**: the same `print` accepts a `std::string`, a substring (`s.substr(0,5)`), a C string, even a buffer slice — anything convertible to a (pointer, length) pair. **(3) Cheap pass-by-value**: a `string_view` is 16 bytes on x64; it fits in two registers. A `const std::string&` requires the caller to have a real `std::string` in memory.
answer.ro: Trei motive. **(1) Fara alocare** pentru literalul de sir: `const std::string&` ar forta compilatorul sa construiasca un `std::string("hello")` temporar, care aloca si copiaza 5 octeti plus terminator null. `string_view` doar impacheteaza pointerul + lungimea literalului — zero alocare. **(2) Flexibilitate de proprietate a buffer-ului**: acelasi `print` accepta un `std::string`, un subsir (`s.substr(0,5)`), un sir C, chiar o felie de buffer — orice convertibil la o pereche (pointer, lungime). **(3) Pass-by-value ieftin**: un `string_view` este 16 octeti pe x64; incape in doua registre. Un `const std::string&` cere ca apelantul sa aiba deja un `std::string` real in memorie.

question.en: You have `std::string_view sv = s.substr(2, 3);` where `s` is `std::string`. You then call `printf("%s", sv.data());`. What happens?
